sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Clifton, NJ?
sections.html:
In Clifton, no closing can take place without a valid dwelling certificate from the Fire Prevention Bureau, and the city has also been revaluing property, which affects assessed values. Those two facts shape how long a sale takes more than the listing itself does.

Clifton is the second-largest city in Passaic County and a bedroom community for New York, with more than a dozen named neighborhoods ranging from Botany Village to Montclair Heights. A seller here usually owns a one- or two-family house or a condo, and the same city paperwork follows the property whether you list it, sell it yourself or accept an offer from an investor. Below is the process in order.

sections.h2: Where is Clifton and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Clifton covers about 11.3 square miles in Passaic County, with the Passaic River along its northeastern edge and Route 3 across the southern part. European settlement dates to 1679, when a Lenape leader deeded about 11,000 acres along the river to Hans Frederick. The city took its name from the cliffs of Garret Mountain, was incorporated on April 26, 1917 to replace Acquackanonk Township, and for decades was farmland. A federal animal quarantine station operated here from 1903 until the late 1970s, and three small working farms remain.

The neighborhoods are distinct, and buyers ask for them by name.

  • Main Mall is the downtown, and Allwood is the other business district, along Route 3.
  • Athenia and Delawanna each have a train station, and Dutch Hill sits near downtown.
  • Botany Village is the northernmost neighborhood, and Lakeview runs along the western edge.
  • Montclair Heights and Rosemawr are among the wealthier residential areas, with Albion Place beside Garret Mountain Reservation.

Census Bureau QuickFacts shows a city of 91,127 people in mid-2025, up from 90,296 in the 2020 count. The owner-occupied rate is 59.6 percent, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $461,900, and median gross rent is $1,711. Median household income is $98,237, and about 35 percent of residents were born abroad. Those numbers describe a city where about four in ten homes are not owner-occupied, so many sellers are landlords as well as owner-occupants.

sections.h2: How do Clifton's highways, trains and schools affect a sale?
sections.html:
Clifton is crossed by Route 3, Route 21, Route 19 and U.S. Route 46, and the Garden State Parkway runs through the city with interchanges 153 through 156. NJ Transit trains stop at Clifton station and Delawanna station on the Main Line toward Hoboken and Suffern. Buses on the 190, 191, 192 and 195 routes go to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and routes 13, 27 and 72 go to Newark. The Census Bureau's mean commute is 28.3 minutes.

Clifton Public Schools runs 18 schools and about 10,500 students, as of the 2020 to 2021 data, with numbered elementary schools, Christopher Columbus and Woodrow Wilson Middle Schools, and Clifton High School. A listing that names the elementary school number and the nearest station answers two of the first questions buyers ask.

sections.h2: How do you get the Clifton dwelling certificate for a sale?
sections.html:
You file a dwelling application with the Fire Prevention Bureau, at 900 Clifton Avenue, after checking with the Building Department that the property has no open permits. The city's instructions give the steps in order, and the application must be signed by both the seller and the buyer.

  • Call the Building Department at 973-470-5809 to confirm there are no open permits and to learn where to get the application stamped.
  • Bring the stamped application, payment and, if you use unverified digital signatures, a copy of the sales contract to Clifton Fire Headquarters. An after-hours drop box is available.
  • Inspections are scheduled on Wednesdays from 9 a.m. to noon, and an adult over 18 has to be present with every area of the structure accessible.
  • Call about seven business days after the inspection, since certificates must be picked up in person.

The certificate depends on passing the building, tax and zoning departments, and it expires six months after the fire department inspection, so schedule it after you have a signed contract and a target closing. The fee schedule on the packet is below.

Clifton dwelling certificate fees, per unit, City of Clifton Fire Prevention Bureau
ServiceFee
Sale certificate, standard$125
Rental certificate, standard$75
Expedited, available within 4 to 20 days$200
Expedited, available within 4 business days$300

Fees are charged per dwelling unit, so a two-family house costs double. Payment can be by personal check, money order, cashier's check, exact-change cash or credit card with a transaction fee, and everything is payable to the City of Clifton. The city will not accept an application without payment or payment without an application.

sections.h2: What alarm and safety items does a Clifton inspector check?
sections.html:
The inspector checks smoke detectors, carbon monoxide alarms and a label for homes with backup power, so fix these before the appointment. Failing and rescheduling costs time on a closing calendar that already depends on a Wednesday slot.

  • Smoke detectors on every level, except crawl spaces and unfinished attics reached by pull-down stairs.
  • A detector within 10 feet of the outside of each bedroom door on any floor that has bedrooms.
  • All detectors under 10 years old, with 10-year sealed batteries when battery operated, and hardwired systems kept in service.
  • Carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas, with more on each additional floor that has sleeping areas.
  • A central station fire alarm tested beforehand, with the test record from a certified company handed over, because inspectors do not test those systems and a missing report fails the inspection.

One- and two-family homes also need a label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter warning about secondary power sources such as generators, solar panels or battery storage. The Fire Prevention Bureau supplies and installs that label on the day of your inspection, so owners with solar should know it is coming.

sections.h2: How does Clifton's revaluation change what a seller should expect?
sections.html:
Clifton has been carrying out a city-wide revaluation, described on the assessor's page and in a city presentation from January 2026. The presentation lists the criteria for a revaluation, including a last revaluation in 1991 and an average ratio of 31.87. A ratio that low indicates assessments sit well below market value, so new values are expected to be higher while the tax rate is meant to fall.

The city's explanation is that a revaluation does not raise the total amount collected. The levy is set by the school, county and municipal budgets, and revaluation spreads it according to value. The presentation's illustration, labeled as an example only, shows a house assessed at $180,000 rising to $540,000 while the rate drops by a factor of three, leaving the bill about the same. Your own result depends on whether your house moved more or less than the city average.

For a seller, that means the assessed value printed on old paperwork may not match the new notice. The state sets the appeal deadline at April 1, or May 1 in a newly revalued municipality, and the presentation adds that an appeal has to prove value with comparable sales. Call the assessing department at 973-470-5838 for your property record.

sections.h2: When are Clifton taxes due and what relief exists?
sections.html:
Clifton taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten-day grace period. The tax collector is at 900 Clifton Avenue, first floor, phone 973-470-5830. The city accepts online payment by e-check only, and there is a lockbox at City Hall for mailed or dropped-off payments, with no cash accepted there. A $35 fee applies to a returned check from wrong account numbers.

The assessor's page lists a $250 deduction for qualifying veterans or surviving spouses and a $250 deduction for seniors or disabled persons. The senior deduction requires age 65 or older, ownership and residence in the house, and annual income of $10,000 or less after permitted exclusions. The tax collector's page also links to the state's ANCHOR program for homeowners and renters. If you receive any of these, tell your closing attorney so the adjustments are right.

sections.h2: Where is a Clifton deed recorded and what does the clerk require?
sections.html:
A Clifton deed is recorded with the Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division, 401 Grand Street, Room 113, in Paterson, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. The office does not do title searches, and it does not record surveys. The county lists specific requirements:

  • Deeds must carry the words Prepared by, the tax block, lot and consideration.
  • Every document needs a record and return address, and original signatures with names printed beneath.
  • Use the official county cover sheet, or pay an extra $20 per document.
  • Pay the realty transfer fee with an attorney trust check, title agency trust check, certified check or cash.

The county also posts the seller forms you need: the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, the Seller Residency Certification, the Nonresident Seller Tax Declaration and the waiver form. A Clifton owner who has moved out of New Jersey is treated as a nonresident for the sale, which can mean an estimated payment at closing, while a federal principal residence exclusion may shelter up to $250,000 of gain, or $500,000 for a qualifying couple.

faqs.q: Can I close on a Clifton house without a dwelling certificate?
faqs.a: No. The city's instructions state that no closing shall take place without a valid Certificate of Inspection, and the certificate expires six months after the fire department inspection.

faqs.q: How much does a Clifton sale certificate cost?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $125 per unit for a sale. Expedited service costs $200 per unit for a 4 to 20 day turnaround or $300 per unit for four business days.

faqs.q: When does the Clifton fire department inspect?
faqs.a: Inspections run on Wednesdays between 9 a.m. and noon, and an adult over 18 must be home. Call about seven business days afterward, because certificates are picked up in person.

faqs.q: When are Clifton property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten-day grace period. Online payment is by e-check only.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Clifton assessment?
faqs.a: The state deadline is April 1, or May 1 in a municipality that has just been revalued. Clifton's revaluation presentation says an appeal must prove value with comparable sales.
